subject: giraffe
pitch: A young reticulated giraffe. Chestnut patches outlined by bright cream lines all over its body and neck, a short mane of stiff brown hair down the neck, two fuzzy ossicones with black tufts on top, big ears, long lashes, a long dark tongue just peeking out, and slender legs fading to cream above the hooves.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the proportions for a young giraffe model, aiming for roughly 2.6 meters tall, and sketching the skeleton structure with pelvis-to-chest spine, neck chain, head, jaw, legs, and tail before defining coordinates.

For coloring, I'm designing a paint function that blends cream underbelly tones with chestnut reticulated patches, using a smoothstep gradient for the legs and a patches function with polygonal shapes and thin gaps to mimic the giraffe's distinctive coat pattern.

Now I'm planning the skeleton: a root joint at the pelvis, with a spine chain of polyline points running from rump to chest, followed by a longer neck chain curving upward and forward through several joints to the head, naming each segment along the way.

I'm separating the head into its own joint parented to the top of the neck chain, angled forward-down, then thinking about how to skin the body using sweeps along the spine and neck chains with varying radii to form the torso and neck surfaces.

Now I'm working out the torso's radius profile across the spine chain from rump to chest, sizing the width and height at each point with sine-based curves for a natural taper, and planning round end caps before moving on to the four legs.

For the front legs, I'm plotting a chain from shoulder down through knee, fetlock, to hoof, naming each joint point and sweeping a tapering radius along a polyline path so corners get smoothed into fillets automatically.

Still planning leg geometry...

I'm mapping out the hind leg joints with hip, stifle, hock, and fetlock points, mirroring left/right with a sign flag, then deciding each leg chain should parent explicitly to the nearest spine segment rather than relying on default nearest-joint behavior.

For the leg geometry I'm tapering the radius from hip to fetlock so it blends into the body smoothly, then building a tail chain from rump to tip with a tapering sweep radius and a darker tuft shape capping the end, using a Catmull path through four points for a natural curve.

Now I'm moving to the head, attaching it to the neck bone and orienting the giraffe's elongated skull forward and slightly downward from the joint.

Building out the loft stations for the upper skull from brow to muzzle, then setting up a separate lower jaw loft with its own joint placement under the cheek.

Now I'm working through the neck path coordinates from base to head joint, checking that total height adds up reasonably for a young giraffe once ossicones and legs are factored in.

For the head itself I'm placing skull cross-sections from the back of the skull forward to the muzzle, shaping the taper with a Catmull spline, then planning the nose pads and nostril spheres with a cream-to-dark gradient for the head coloring.

Now I'm setting up the lower jaw as a separate joint with its own loft cross-sections, checking the vertical gap between upper and lower jaw at the mouth line so there's room for the tongue to peek through without leaving an unwanted hole.

Making the tongue droop and peek out past the muzzle tip, bound to the jaw bone so it moves naturally with the mouth, using a curved path with a flattened cross-section. Now moving to the eyes, placing a big dark sphere on each side of the head.

Placing 6 lashes per eye along an arc from the eye center, angled upward and outward to follow the skull's curvature, then moving on to designing the ears.

For the ears, I'm shaping leaf-like extruded outlines oriented outward and slightly upward, defining a local coordinate frame so the extrusion axis points outward-up while the cross-section stays squared off, with a thin bevel for softness.

Color-wise, I'll give the ear a brown rim with a pink interior by layering two extrusions—one slightly smaller for the inner color—so both faces show the pink tone while the outer edge reads as brown.

Now I'm positioning the ears and skull bones, placing the ear root near the top of the skull, then setting up the ossicones as two small cylinders angled slightly backward with black tufted spheres on top, giving them a tan-brown fuzzy base color.

Still designing the tuft spikes...

I should also add a small median forehead bump typical of giraffes, plus dark nostril spheres positioned near the muzzle tip, calculating their placement based on the cap's rounded end.

Now for the mane: I want stiff brown hair running along the dorsal side of the neck, following the neck sweep path. I'll use spike geometry rather than texture cards for safety, placing each spike outward along the normal direction at points traced along the neck curve.

Mane tufts get slight jitter and vary in length, extending partway along the neck in dark brown, while the spike base keeps a rigid color with a count around 22. The neck sweep runs the coat color along a radius function from root to tip, tilted forward about 30 degrees, with hooves, chest, and belly shading handled by the same continuous paint object across the whole figure.

I'm bumping the paint sheet resolution to 2048 for finer detail across the torso, neck, legs, tail, and head, each painted separately with cream fades and patches. The tail gets a tapering radius with a dark spike tuft at the end, while I skip extra details like hip bumps, eyebrows, and udder for now. I'm naming the leg joint chains, working out front legs as shoulder-elbow/carpus-fetlock-hoof and puzzling over how to distinguish the rear hip-knee naming from the front without conflicts.

Working out joint naming...

Still shaping leg proportions...

Defining the torso spine path with pelvis, spine1, and spine2 joints, then shaping the body's varying width and height from rump to chest for a deeper chest profile.

Working out the neck's radius taper from its base to head and placing the neck chain of four points starting at the chest-neck junction, parented under spine2, with tangents guiding the curve upward.

I'm also setting ground contact so hoof cylinders sit flush at y=0, positioning front and rear hooves along the z-axis, and sketching out the tail's Catmull-Rom chain starting from the rear hip area.

For the tail tuft, I'm adding a small downward spike at the chain's end, and considering eye size (larger for a young giraffe, around 0.045 radius) and a dark tongue bone sticking out visibly from the front.

I'm skipping teeth and lips for now, focusing on the rig roles (spine, neck, leg, tail, head, jaw) and setting up the import statements and coat patch generation using the builder's patches and paint utilities to create the giraffe's spotted texture.

Writing coat blending logic...

I'm defining head paint so patches dominate the back of the skull while a tan-to-dark-muzzle gradient takes over toward the face, blended by a z-based smoothstep, and reusing that same paint for the jaw. Then I'm starting the mane geometry, sweeping points along the neck curve and working out tangent/axis directions for each strand.

Still working out mane strand directions and staggered rows...

Now moving to the ears, I'm defining a function that computes outward and forward direction vectors to extrude the ear shape from the head.

Still building ossicone geometry...

Defining head and jaw joints...

Writing leg chains...

Working out the torso sweep from the spine chain, then setting up the paint resolution and checking loft/sweep options for the head bone and tongue geometry. Now I'm computing eyelash placement, figuring out the eye center position based on skull width at that z-coordinate so the lashes radiate correctly from the eye socket.

Now I'm placing a small white highlight sphere offset from the eye center to give it that glossy look, then I'll finalize the code.
